name: Antigua Taberna Queirolo
summary: Lima's best-documented criollo institution: an 1880 taberna with a large local following. Go for old-Lima atmosphere and honest classics (cau cau, papa rellena, butifarra, picarones), not refined cooking.

value.text: Mon-Wed 8:00-22:00, Thu to 23:00, Fri-Sat to midnight, Sun 8:00-17:00.
About S/150-220 (~US$45-65) for two with a main each, a shared starter and drinks (my estimate)

facts.value: Comida criolla / Lima home-style taberna plus pisco bar

items.name: Cau cau (S/40)
items.description: Home-style tripe stew with rice, a house specialty.

items.name: Ají de gallina (S/39)
items.description: Shredded chicken in creamy yellow-chili sauce.

items.name: Lomo saltado (S/53)
items.description: Wok-fried beef, onion, tomato, fries and rice.

items.name: Causa acebichada / langostinos (S/37)

items.name: Mondongo

items.name: Escabeche de pescado
items.description: Fried fish in onion and ají pickle.

items.name: Sánguche de jamón del país (butifarra)
items.description: House ham sandwich with salsa criolla; signature.

value.format: Historic all-day taberna (c.1880), marble tables, à la carte
pros: Wide classic menu at moderate prices
Pisco shop attached; easy to pair with Museo Larco
cons: Slow service and noise at peak
Some dishes made early, some call food 'mid'
accolades: Frommer's: one of Lima's oldest continuously operating bars
Pueblo Libre municipality and MINCETUR heritage inventories (founded 1880)
value.how_to_book: Form says reservations are confirmed by email; WhatsApp also listed. Needed only for weekend dinner or groups; 2 people can usually walk in at weekday lunch.
